"Mom! Dad! Help!" Tom and Jen shout. They are scared and sad.

Mom and Dad wake up too. They see the truck and the van. They run out of the van and wave their arms.

"Stop! Stop! That is our home!" Mom and Dad yell.

The truck driver sees them and stops. He gets out of the truck and walks to them.

"Sorry, folks. I did not know you were in there. I have to take this van. It is old and broken. The city says so." The truck driver says.

"But this is our home. We have nowhere else to go. Please, let us keep it." Mom and Dad beg.

The truck driver looks at them and sees their humble clothes and faces. He feels sorry for them. He thinks for a moment.

"OK, OK. I will make a deal with you. You can keep the van, but you have to move it to a different place. A place where the city will not bother you. Do you have such a place?" The truck driver asks.

Mom and Dad think hard. They remember their friend Bob. Bob has a farm in the country. He has a lot of space and animals. He is kind and generous. He might let them stay there.

"Yes, we have a place. Our friend Bob has a farm. He will let us stay there. Can you take us there?" Mom and Dad ask.

The truck driver nods. He hooks the van back to the truck. He helps Mom and Dad and Tom and Jen get in the van. He starts the truck and drives away.

Tom and Jen are happy. They hug Mom and Dad and thank the truck driver. They look forward to seeing Bob and his farm. They hope they will be happy there.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to tell Rex to stop, but she was afraid he would hurt her. She wished he would leave her alone.

"You have to eat your vegetables, Tommy. They are good for you. They make you strong and healthy," his mom said, urging him to take a bite.

"But I don't like them. They taste bad. Can I have some juice instead?" Tommy asked, pushing his plate away.

"No, you can't have juice. You can have water or milk. And you can't have dessert until you finish your vegetables. Come on, Tommy, it's not that hard. Just try one bite and see if you like it," his mom said, picking up a fork and a green bean.

She held it near his mouth and smiled. Tommy looked at the green bean and felt scared. He did not want to eat it. He wanted to run away and play with his toys. He shook his head and closed his mouth.

"Please, Tommy, just one bite. For me. I promise you will like it. It's crunchy and sweet. And if you eat it, you can have a cookie later," his mom said, trying to be nice.

Tommy looked at his mom and saw that she was sad. He did not want to make her sad. He loved his mom. He opened his mouth and let her put the green bean in. He chewed it and swallowed it. It was not as bad as he thought. It was a little dry, but it was also crunchy and sweet.

"See, Tommy, that wasn't so bad, was it? Do you want another one?" his mom asked, holding another green bean.

Tommy nodded and took another one. He ate it and smiled. He liked green beans. He ate some more and then some carrots. He finished his plate and felt proud.

"Good job, Tommy! I'm so proud of you. You ate all your vegetables. You are a big boy. Now you can have your dessert. What do you want?" his mom asked, hugging him.

"I want a cookie, please. And some milk. And some more green beans," Tommy said, surprising his mom.

"More green beans? Really? You like them that much?" his mom asked, laughing.

"Yes, mom. I like them. They are good for me. They make me strong and healthy. And they are crunchy and sweet," Tommy said, repeating his mom's words.

"Okay, then. You can have some more green beans. And a cookie. And some milk. You are a very good boy, Tommy. I love you," his mom said, kissing him.

Emma felt encouraged. She smiled and waved goodbye to the swan, feeling reassured that being kind would fill her heart with joy. From that moment on, Emma never shivered in loneliness again.

"Sure, let's try it. Maybe it will make us skip faster and higher," Ben said.

They took turns to skip with the new rope, and had a lot of fun. But then, a girl came over and looked angry. She said, "Hey, that's my rope! You took it from my bag! Give it back to me!"

Anna and Ben were surprised and scared. They did not know it was someone else's rope. They thought it was a gift from the park.

"We're sorry, we didn't know. We thought it was for everyone to use," Anna said.

"Well, it's not. It's mine, and it's very special. My grandma gave it to me for my birthday. It's not nice to take things that don't belong to you," the girl said.

Anna and Ben felt bad. They realized they had made a mistake. They gave the rope back to the girl, and said they were sorry again.

The girl smiled and said, "It's okay, I forgive you. But next time, ask before you use something that's not yours. And you know what? You don't need a luxury rope to skip. Any rope will do, as long as you have fun and be smart. Skipping is good for your body and your mind. Do you want to skip with me?"

Anna and Ben nodded, and said yes. They joined the girl, and skipped with their old ropes. They learned a lesson that day: it's better to share and be honest, than to take and be greedy. And they made a new friend, too.

"Look, I made a dog!" Lily said, showing Sam her block dog. It had four legs, a tail, and a head with two ears.

"That's nice, Lily. But I made something better. I made a rocket!" Sam said, pointing to his block rocket. It had a cone, a cylinder, and four fins.

Lily and Sam started to argue. They both thought their block creation was the best. They did not want to share or play together.

"Your rocket is silly. It can't fly. My dog is real. It can bark and run." Lily said.

"Your dog is boring. It can't go to space. My rocket is cool. It can blast off and see the stars." Sam said.

They were very serious and angry. They did not have fun.

Then, Mom came in. She saw Lily and Sam fighting over the blocks. She was not happy.

"Stop, Lily and Sam. Why are you fighting? You have so many blocks. You can create anything you want. Why don't you work together and make something new?" Mom said.

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They felt sorry. They did not want to fight. They wanted to be friends.

"Sorry, Lily. Your dog is nice. Can I pet it?" Sam said.

"Sorry, Sam. Your rocket is cool. Can I ride it?" Lily said.

They smiled and hugged. They decided to create something new with the blocks. They made a dog-rocket. It had a dog head, a rocket body, and a tail that could shoot fire.

"Wow, this is awesome!" Lily and Sam said.

They played with their dog-rocket. They pretended it could fly to the moon and meet other dogs. They had fun.

Mom was happy. She saw Lily and Sam playing nicely with the blocks. She was proud of them. She gave them a kiss and a cookie.

Jack was unsure. He asked his mom: "Can we take the monster with us?" His mom replied, "No, we can't take it on the trip, Jack." Jack thought for a moment and then asked again, "Why not?" 

His mom said, "Jack, it is important to identify what is important to have with you and what you do not need. We cannot take the monster on our trip because it is too big! When we take things with us on a trip, we must be sure that it is necessary to bring."

Jack understood, and he and his mom continued to unpack. Jack knew that while it was fun to have things with him on his trip, it was important to recognize what he really needed.

"Maybe. But we have to be quiet and gentle. Parrots are shy and scared of loud noises." Mom says.

Mom, Sara and Ben walk slowly to the tree. They watch the parrot with their eyes. The parrot watches them back. It tilts its head and opens its beak.

"Hello, hello!" The parrot says.

Sara and Ben gasp. They laugh and clap their hands.

"Hello, parrot!" Sara says.

"Hello, parrot!" Ben says.

The parrot repeats their words. It flaps its wings and hops on the branch.

"Wow, the parrot can talk!" Sara says.

"Yes, it can. It learned the words from people. It is a very clever bird." Mom says.

Sara and Ben want to touch the parrot. They reach out their hands. But the parrot is scared. It flies away from the tree. It lands on Mom's shoulder. It nibbles her ear.

"Ouch, ouch!" Mom says.

"Sorry, sorry!" The parrot says.

Sara and Ben giggle. They think the parrot is funny. They say goodbye to the parrot. They hope to see it again. They hug Mom and thank her for taking them to the park. They have a lot of fun.

"We did, sir," Tom said.

"We wanted to surprise our mom," Anna said.

Suddenly, her mom appeared. "Honey, you mustn't touch the ice," her mom warned. "It's too dangerous."

The little girl pouted. She felt so disappointed that she wouldn't be able to touch the ice. 

But then her mom softened. "I'll tell you what," she said. "You can observe the ice. stand here, watch it, and enjoy the view, OK?"

The little girl was eager to try out her mother's suggestion. She kept her eye on the ice, looking for all the different shapes and colors. She was fascinated and she couldn't keep a smile from coming to her face. 

The little girl and her mom happily walked home, and the little girl always remembered the day she got to observe the ice.

"Go away, dog!" Sam shouted. "This is our tree!"

The dog did not listen. It ran towards Sam and Lily. They ran away, too. They looked for a place to hide. They saw a bench near a pond. They ran to the bench and climbed on it.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Sam asked.

"Yes, I'm okay, Sam," Lily said. "But I'm sad. We can't play in our fort now. The dog took our tree."

Sam hugged Lily. He was sad, too. He loved their fort. He wished the dog would leave.

Then, they heard a whistle. They looked and saw a man. The man was calling the dog. The dog stopped barking and growling. It ran to the man. The man put a leash on the dog. He smiled at Sam and Lily.

"I'm sorry, kids," the man said. "My dog is not mean, but he is very loyal. He thought you were trying to take his tree. He likes to play there, too. He did not mean to scare you."

Sam and Lily felt better. They understood. The dog was not bad, just loyal. They smiled back at the man.

"Can we share the tree?" Sam asked.

"Of course, you can," the man said. "My dog is friendly, too. He likes to make new friends. Do you want to pet him?"

Sam and Lily nodded. They got off the bench and walked to the man and the dog. The dog wagged his tail and licked their faces. Sam and Lily laughed. They petted the dog and gave him a treat.

They became friends with the man and the dog. They played together in the park. They shared the tree and the fort. They had fun. They were happy. They were loyal.

Mommy smiles and says, "Oh, my darlings, you are both helpful and silly. You have gas because you blew the balloon too much. It is not good for your tummy. Next time, blow less and share more. So Sarah and Cleo watched the sun set together. They talked about their days and laughed at funny things that had happened. The sun went down and the stars came out, and Sarah and Cleo smiled at each other in the cozy evening.

Once upon a time there was a small green frog called Luther who lived in a pond under a thicket of trees. One day, he heard some noise coming from the pond and he decided to explore it. 

He came across an old tree with a box underneath it. He thought it was a little odd, so he hopped closer to take a better look. He opened the lid of the box and saw something wrapped in a blanket. It was cold to the touch.

Luther jumped back and said, "Who is that?"

A quiet voice said, "It's me. I'm Jack. I value your kindness."

Luther was surprised because he did not expect to find a person inside the box. He said, "It's my pleasure. Do you need help or food?"

"I need a warm wrap and a comfortable place to sleep," said Jack.

"Come with me," Luther replied. "I know just the place."

Together, they hopped out of the pond and found a cosy spot nearby. Luther found Jack some warm clothes and tucked him into a soft blanket. When they were done, Luther said, "Goodnight, Jack. I'm so glad I could help." 

Jack smiled and said, "Me too. Thank you."

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy trucks. They had a big pile of sand in the backyard, and they pretended to be builders. They used their trucks to load and unload the sand, and made roads and hills and castles.

One day, it was very hot and sunny, and they got sweaty and dirty from playing. Their mom called them inside and said, "It's time for a shower, boys. You need to wash off the sand and cool down." But Tom and Sam did not want to stop playing. They said, "No, mom, we want to play more. We are not dirty, we are builders."

Their mom was not happy. She said, "You are not builders, you are boys. And boys need to listen to their mom and take a shower. If you don't, you will get itchy and smelly and have bad dreams. Now come on, or I will take away your trucks."

Tom and Sam did not like that. They did not want to lose their trucks. But they were also restless and wanted to play more. They thought of a plan. They said, "OK, mom, we will take a shower. But can we take our trucks with us? They are dirty too, and they need a shower."

Their mom thought for a moment. She said, "Well, I guess you can, but only if you promise to wash them well and not make a mess in the bathroom. And you have to be quick, because it's almost time for dinner."

Tom and Sam agreed. They ran to the bathroom with their trucks, and turned on the shower. They put their trucks under the water, and pretended to wash them. But they also splashed and sprayed and made a lot of noise. They had fun, but they also made the bathroom wet and sandy.

Their mom heard the noise and came to check on them. She was not happy. She said, "Boys, what are you doing? You are not taking a shower, you are making a mess. Look at the floor, and the walls, and the towels. They are all wet and sandy. And you are still dirty. You did not wash yourselves, you only played with your trucks."

Tom and Sam felt ashamed. They knew they did not listen to their mom, and they did not do what they said. They said, "Sorry, mom, we were having fun. We did not mean to make a mess. We will clean it up, and we will take a real shower."

Their mom said, "You better do that, boys. And next time, when I tell you to do something, you do it. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We will do better next time. We love you, mom."

Their mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, boys. Now go and take a shower, and then come for dinner. And don't forget to dry your trucks."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and do what she says. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home.

One day, he was awoken by a voice. It was a number! The number said, "Hey pipe! Wake up! Let's go exploring!". The pipe sighed and replied, "No thanks. I'm too lazy to move." 

But the number was persistent. He said, "Come on, pipe! Moving will make you feel better, I promise!"

The pipe thought about it for a minute, and then decided to give it a try. So, he moved his long body around and even danced a bit. He was surprised to find that he actually enjoyed it!

So, from then on the lazy pipe and the number went on many fun adventures. No matter what, the pipe was always happy to go exploring with his friend.

Anna is sad. She says, "I will miss you too. When will you come back?"

Tom says, "I don't know. Maybe in a long time. But we can talk on the phone sometimes."

Anna nods. She gives Tom a hug and a kiss. She says, "Bye, Tom. Have a good trip."

Tom and his family get in the car and drive away. Anna waves to them. She feels lonely. She goes to her room and looks at her toys. She does not want to play with them. She wants to play with Tom. She makes a wish. She says, "I wish Tom was here. I wish we could play together again."

She sees a star in the sky. She thinks it is a magic star. She says, "Star, star, please hear my wish. Please bring Tom back to me. Please make us happy."

The star twinkles. It hears Anna's wish. It sends a message to Tom. It says, "Tom, Tom, Anna misses you. She wishes you were here. She wants to play with you again."

Tom hears the message. He feels happy. He says, "Star, star, thank you for telling me. I miss Anna too. I wish I was there. I want to play with her again."

He tells his parents. He says, "Mom, Dad, can we go back to Anna? She is my best friend. I don't want to be away from her."

His parents are surprised. They say, "But Tom, we are going to a very nice place. It is very rich and beautiful. You will have a lot of fun there."

Tom says, "I don't care about rich and beautiful. I care about Anna. She is more fun than anything. Please, can we go back?"

His parents see that Tom is very serious. They love Tom. They want him to be happy. They say, "OK, Tom, we will go back. We will see Anna again."

Tom is very happy. He says, "Thank you, Mom, Dad. You are the best. And thank you, star, for helping me."

He calls Anna on the phone. He says, "Anna, Anna, guess what? I am coming back. We can play together again. I am so happy."

Anna is very happy too. She says, "Tom, Tom, really? You are coming back? I am so happy too. I can't wait to see you."

They both smile. They both say, "I love you, best friend."

The star smiles too. It says, "You are welcome, Tom and Anna. You are very good friends. I am glad I could make your wish come true."

"Maybe it went back to the dirt," Ben said.

But Lily did not listen. She saw a gray cat in a pet shop. She loved cats. She ran to the cat and said, "Hello, kitty, you are so cute. Can I pet you?" She opened the cage and took the cat out. The cat was scared and angry. It scratched Lily's face and ran away.

Lily cried. She was in pain and she was sorry. She looked for Mom, but she could not see her. She saw many people and things, but not Mom. She felt alone and scared. She wanted Mom to protect her.

Mom heard Lily's cry. She was worried and angry. She ran to the pet shop and saw Lily's face. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You are hurt and you are naughty. You did not stay with me. You made the cat run away. You are in trouble."

She took Lily to the nurse. The nurse cleaned Lily's face and put a bandage on it. She said, "Lily, you have to be careful and listen to your mom. The cat was not your friend. It was wild and scared. You have to respect animals and their homes."

Lily was sad. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, nurse. I'm sorry, cat. I just wanted to play. I love you, Mom. Please don't be mad at me."

Mom hugged Lily. She said, "I love you, too, Lily. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to obey me and stay with me. I want to protect you and keep you safe. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I will be good. Can we go home now?"

Mom said, "Yes, Lily. We can go home now. But you have to say sorry to the pet shop owner and pay for the cat's cage. And you have to be more careful next time."

Lily said, "OK, Mom. I will say sorry and pay. And I will be more careful. I don't want to get hurt or lose you again."

They left the mall. Lily was still sad and sore. She did not like the mall anymore. She learned a hard lesson. She wished she had listened to Mom. The end.

Her mom and dad said, "OK, but be careful. Don't go too far. Stay where we can see you."

Lucy said, "OK, I will." But she did not listen. She was very independent. She wanted to explore. She walked and walked along the beach. She found many pebbles. She filled her pocket with pebbles.

She did not notice that she was far from her mom and dad. She did not notice that the sun was going down. She did not notice that the tide was coming in. She did not notice that she was lost.

She looked around and saw that she was alone. She did not see her mom and dad. She did not see any people. She only saw water and sand and rocks. She was scared. She cried, "Mom! Dad! Where are you?"

She heard a voice. It was her mom. She said, "Lucy, where are you? We are looking for you. We are worried about you."

Lucy said, "Mom, I'm here. I'm sorry. I went too far. I wanted to get pebbles. Please find me."

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lucy. We are coming. Stay where you are. We love you."

Lucy waited and waited. She saw a light. It was her dad. He had a flashlight. He found her and hugged her. He said, "Lucy, we are so glad you are safe. You scared us. Why did you go so far?"

Lucy said, "I'm sorry, dad. I was independent. I wanted to get pebbles. But I learned my lesson. I will not go far again. I will listen to you and mom."

Her dad said, "That's good, Lucy. We are proud of you for being independent. But you also need to be careful and responsible. You need to follow the rules and stay close to us. We are here to protect you and help you. We are a team."

Lucy said, "I understand, dad. I love you and mom. Thank you for finding me."

They walked back to their car. Lucy gave her mom and dad some of her pebbles. She said, "These are for you. They are from the beach. They are beautiful and special. Just like you."

Her mom and dad smiled and thanked her. They said, "We love you, Lucy. You are beautiful and special. Just like your pebbles."

The end.

"Mom, I made you something!" Anna called out.

Mom came into the kitchen and saw the pot on the stove. She smiled and hugged Anna.

"Thank you, sweetie, what did you make?" Mom asked.

"I made you soup, Mom. I used water and salt and pepper and sugar. Do you want to try it?" Anna said proudly.

Mom looked at the pot and saw the water was boiling and bubbling. She turned off the stove and took the pot off the heat.

"Wow, Anna, you are very creative. But you know, we have to be careful when we use the stove. It can be very hot and dangerous. Next time, you can ask me to help you, okay?" Mom said gently.

"Okay, Mom. I'm sorry. I just wanted to make you happy. I love you, Mom." Anna said.

"I love you too, Anna. And I appreciate your generous gift. But you know what? I think this soup is too spicy and sweet for me. Maybe we can share it with the birds outside. They might like it more." Mom suggested.

"Okay, Mom. Let's do that. Maybe the birds will love it too." Anna agreed.

They poured the soup into a bowl and took it outside. They put the bowl on the grass and watched as the birds came and pecked at the soup. Anna and Mom laughed and clapped as they saw the birds enjoy the soup.

"See, Anna, you made the birds happy too. You are a very kind and generous girl. And I love you very much." Mom said.

"I love you too, Mom. And I love the birds. And I love the soup. And I love the pot." Anna said.

"Books are boring. Puddles are fun. Come on, Mia. Please," Tom begs.

"No, Tom. I like books. Books are quiet. Puddles are loud. And wet. And cold. No, thank you," Mia says.

He opens the door. He runs to the puddle. He jumps in it. He splashes. He laughs.

"Tom, come back! You are wet! You will get sick!" Mia shouts.

She drops her book. She runs to the door. She sees Tom. He is wet. He is cold. He is not laughing. He is sneezing.

"Tom, I told you so. You are sick. You need to come in. You need to get warm. You need to rest," Mia says.

She gets another towel. She wraps it around Tom. She rubs his hair. She rubs his arms. She rubs his legs. She rubs his feet. She is a good friend.

"Sorry, Mia. You were right. Books are better. Puddles are bad. Can you read to me?" Tom says.

"Sure, Tom. I will read to you. But next time, listen to me. And to Mom. Rain is not for playing. Rain is for staying in," Mia says.

They go inside. They sit on the couch. Mia reads to Tom. Tom listens. They are quiet. They are happy. The rain goes on.

Lily ran to the kitchen and saw the fire too. She was scared and asked her mom, "What should we do?" Her mom replied, "We need to replace the water in the pool with sand. That way, the fire won't spread."

Lily and her mom quickly got to work, replacing the water with sand. Soon, the fire was put out and everyone was safe. Lily felt proud that she had helped her mom and saved the house. From that day on, Lily knew that she could do anything if she tried.

Once upon a time, a bald dad was cooking dinner at his house. He stood in the kitchen and cooked the dinner with a big smile on his face.

He cooked some vegetables in the pan, and some meat in the oven. Meanwhile, the back fence of the house was looking a bit old.

So Dad decided to cook dinner first, and then he would fix the fence. He quickly finished cooking dinner and then got to work on the fence. He took some wood and some tools and mended the old fence.
